hints: Differentiate $x=2t+\sin2t$ and $y=1-2\cos2t$ carefully using the chain rule.
Rewrite $\sin2t$ as $2\sin t\cos t$ and $1+\cos2t$ as $2\cos^2t$, then simplify the quotient to the required tangent form.
walkthrough:
Apply the double angle identity $1 + \cos 2t = 2\cos^2 t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 2(2\cos^2 t) = 4\cos^2 t$$

Apply the double angle identity $\sin 2t = 2\sin t \cos t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = 4(2\sin t \cos t) = 8\sin t \cos t$$

Use the parametric derivative rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{8\sin t \cos t}{4\cos^2 t} = \dfrac{2\sin t}{\cos t} = 2\tan t$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Parametric Curves: Identifies a derivative of $x$ or $y$ with respect to $t$; Derives $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4\sin2t}{2+2\cos2t}$, or equivalent; Concludes with $\frac{dy}{dx}=2\tan t$.

hints: Relate normal and tangent gradients by $m_{\rm normal}m_{\rm tangent}=-1$.
With $m_{\rm tangent}=2\tan t$, set the normal gradient equal to $2$ and solve for $t$ in $-\pi/2<t<\pi/2$.
Insert that parameter value into $x=2t+\sin2t$ and give the coordinate to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Express the gradient of the normal $m_N$ in terms of the derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$:
$$m_N = -\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}} = -\dfrac{1}{2\tan t}$$

Set the normal gradient equal to $2$:
$$-\dfrac{1}{2\tan t} = 2$$
$$2\tan t = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\tan t = -\dfrac{1}{4} = -0.25$$

Find the value of $t$ in the interval $-\dfrac{\pi}{2} < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$t = \tan^{-1}(-0.25) \approx -0.2449787 \text{ radians}$$
